previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a patient with multiple myeloma, COPD, CAD, and a history of bladder cancer with neobladder, was admitted from clinic for evaluation of elevated creatinine (2.5) and hypercalcemia. He reported good oral intake and urine output but admitted to inconsistent straight-catheterization and reduced fluid intake. IV fluids were initiated, and he was catheterized three times daily. Renal ultrasound showed no hydronephrosis. Creatinine improved to 1.5, and calcium normalized to 8.3 after IV pamidronate. Anemia (Hct 23.4) was attributed to chronic kidney disease and myeloma, with no active bleeding. Revlimid and Bactrim were held pending oncology follow-up. He remained stable, was discharged home on day 3 with instructions to maintain hydration, adhere to catheterization schedule, and follow up the next day with his oncologist.
